To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the myelin proteins P0, P1, and P2 are differentially altered in sciatic myelins of two mouse mutants, Quaking and jimpy.
the myelin from Quaking mice is severely affected and the myelin from Jimp mice is normal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the myelin proteins in the sciatic nerve from Quaking mice.

the analysis of the protein composition of myelin from two neurological mutant mice: Quaking mice, which are characterized by a severe demyelination, and Jimpy mice, which have a defective oligodendroglial maturation.
the molecular basis of myelin abnormalities in two neurological mutants in the mouse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protein composition of the myelin sheaths of the peripheral nerves is normal in the Jimpy mouse, while in the Quaking mouse it is not.

in the Quaking mouse a primary defect in the synthesis of myelin proteins P0 and P2 is responsible for the myelin deficiency, whereas in the Jimpy mouse a primary defect of myelin protein synthesis is absent.
the myelin of the sciatic nerve in Quaking mice is deficient in the two intrinsic myelin protein P1 and P 2, whereas Jimpy myelin has a normal protein composition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
myelin proteins P0 and P1 are synthesized by oligodendrocytes and that the synthesis of P2 is restricted to Schwann cells.
the myelin protein composition is not altered in Jimpy mice but is drastically changed in sciatic myelinated nerve fibres of Quaking mice.
in both mutants the major myelin proteins P0 and P1 are not affected, whereas the minor myelin proteins P2 and P3 are affected in Quaking mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to the myelin basic protein, there are other proteins in the myelin sheath that play a role in myelin stability.
, in the absence of the myelin basic protein (MBP) gene, the P2 myelin protein is not expressed.

the myelin sheath of peripheral nerves in the Quaking mutant mouse is defective in two intrinsic myelin components, P1 and P 2, whereas in the Jimpy mutant, the myelin sheaths of peripheral nerves appear to be normal in composition.
